definition: The psychological exhaustion users experience from repeatedly encountering consent requests, leading to mindless acceptance of privacy terms without proper consideration.
metaDescription: Learn about consent fatigue - why users get overwhelmed by privacy consent requests and accept terms without reading them, undermining privacy protection.
simpleExplanation: Imagine being asked to make a decision every few minutes throughout your day. Eventually, you'd stop thinking carefully and just say 'yes' to everything. That's consent fatigue - when people get so tired of cookie banners and privacy pop-ups that they automatically click 'Accept All' without reading what they're agreeing to.
whyItMatters: Consent fatigue undermines the entire purpose of privacy laws like GDPR. When users mindlessly accept all tracking and data collection just to make pop-ups go away, they're not making informed choices about their privacy. This creates a false sense of compliance while actually enabling more data collection than ever before.
technicalDetail: Consent fatigue occurs when the cognitive load of processing multiple consent requests exceeds users' decision-making capacity. Research shows that after encountering several privacy notices, users exhibit 'clicking fatigue' and are 40% more likely to accept all cookies regardless of content. This phenomenon is often exploited through dark patterns that make rejecting consent more difficult than accepting.

examples.scenario: Daily web browsing with cookie banners
examples.explanation: A user visits 20 websites in a day, each showing a cookie consent banner. By the 10th site, they stop reading and just click 'Accept All' on every remaining banner to avoid the mental effort of deciding.

After installing several apps that each request location, camera, and contact access, a user becomes overwhelmed and starts granting all permissions without considering whether each app actually needs them.

An online shopper encounters multiple pre-checked boxes for marketing emails, partner offers, and data sharing during checkout. Feeling rushed and overwhelmed, they leave everything checked rather than read each option.
